tool_input.description: Run acceptance CLI on local logs

result:
**WP-19 is PARTIAL.** The analysis script and tests meet the acceptance checks I could run. The written analysis doesn't hold up, so don't act on its fix recommendations yet. The branch is `wp/19` and the report commit is `d30e92d`.

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| Gate | `GATE PASS` (run with `--max-lines 1100`; the 717-line script is over the default limit) |
| Acceptance pytest | `104 passed, 1 skipped in 13.68s` (I ran it) |
| CLI on `logs/vofa` | **Not run by me.** The command was denied and `logs/vofa` isn't in this worktree. The workers say today's rows match your facts, but that is only their claim; please run it. |
| Diff scope | Script and test under `ground_station/research/`, plus `WP-19.md`. The branch also has the worker digests and my task files, as in earlier WPs, so your strict `--stat` check will show those too. |
| Worker rounds | 3/3. The brief named no lane, so I used the usual gemini chain. The VPS Gemini pool ran out in round 1 (resets 2026-10-04), so rounds 2–3 fell back to free Qwen. |

**Where the analysis breaks** (the details are in the status block at the top of `WP-19.md`):
- **H1 "trim over-corrects":** the worker's own table contradicts it. Hover roll is the same on both days (about -1.0 to -1.6°). What changed is the gap between commanded and actual roll: about +1.2 to +1.85° yesterday, about 0 today. So the trim closed that gap; it did not add lean.
- **H2 (bias mismatch):** the raw optical-flow velocity the velocity loop uses isn't logged, so the claimed 3.34 cm/s mismatch rests on an assumption. One real measured change: the optical-flow zero offset is about 2–4 today versus about 0 yesterday, both on the ground and in the air.
- **"40% trim / 60% bias" split and the predicted fix effects:** nothing behind them.
- **Axis mapping:** neither WP-9 nor the drift-investigation doc says what the operator calls "x". The operator needs to define it, e.g. relative to the takeoff heading, before any verdict on the drift's sign is valid.

**Your call:** keep the script (it works) and either re-brief the analysis once Gemini quota is back, with operator "x" defined first, or do the analysis yourself.
